sources.citation: Barsuhn A et al. Training volume increases or maintenance based on previous volume: the effects on muscular adaptations in trained males. J Appl Physiol. 2025;138(1):259–269.
sources.publication_check: Institutional copy of paginated journal article and publisher abstract checked. Direct publisher full text returned 403. No correction surfaced in targeted search; comprehensive notice check remains outstanding.
sources.rights: Institutional metadata reports CC BY 4.0. Confirm version-specific and deployment rights; retain metadata, links and original summaries.
sources.appraisal: Methods, Fig. 1, Tables 1 and 3, Results and Discussion inspected. 55 allocated, 29 completed; available-data mixed models included 55. Group main effect is not difference in change. Unusually narrow reported intervals and discordant pairwise p-values require clarification.

claims.assertion: In the trial of trained men, reported squat strength increased during the intervention including the habitual-set maintenance arm; a differential change between maintenance and volume increases was not established.
claims.limitations: 55 allocated and 29 completed; differing pre/post denominators; baseline imbalance; no significant group-by-time interaction reported; uncertainty reporting requires clarification; not equivalence, optimal dose or hybrid transfer.
claims.assessment: Full journal copy inspected. Retain qualitative interpretation provisionally; verify mixed-model uncertainty, missingness and pairwise contrasts before approval.

support.locator: Results, Maximum Strength and Strength Endurance, p. 265; Table 3 p. 266; Discussion pp. 266–267; Fig. 1 p. 261
support.result: Reported model time effect +21.47 kg (95% CI 21.27 to 21.66, as printed; requires clarification). Control descriptive means 161.90 to 193.70 kg with n=21 and n=10 respectively. No significant group-by-time interaction reported. Direct difference-in-change interval not verified.
support.restriction: Descriptive means with unequal denominators are not paired individual changes. Do not infer superiority or equivalence, individual set threshold or quantitative prescription.
